testName: Class A Knowledge Test #2 50 Questions • Passing Score 40

questions.question: When checking your vehicle, what should you NOT inspect?

options.text: The same tire brand on all tires

questions.correctAnswerText: The same tire brand on all tires
questions.explanation: Before driving, check that your tire air pressure is not too high or too low. The tire brand does not need to match.

questions.question: Where is the safety relief valve usually found?
questions.explanation: The safety relief valve in an air brake system is located in the tank that receives air first from the compressor.

questions.question: When it is hard to see, like at dawn or dusk, how can you make your vehicle more visible?
questions.explanation: When visibility is poor (at dawn, dusk, rain, or snow), turn on your low beam headlights. Do not use high beams when other vehicles are nearby.

questions.question: Why should you look at your tires in your mirrors often?

options.text: To see if the tires are rolling properly
To see if the tread is good enough
To compare tire size to other vehicles

questions.explanation: Check your tires in your mirrors regularly. This helps you spot a tire fire. Tire fires can happen when tires are under-inflated, dual tires touch, or tires overheat.

questions.question: Rough acceleration can:

options.text: Help you stay awake on long trips

questions.explanation: Always speed up slowly and smoothly so your vehicle does not jerk. Rough acceleration can damage your vehicle's parts.

questions.question: If you stop on a one-way or divided highway, how far behind your vehicle should you place warning devices?
questions.explanation: On a one-way or divided highway, place warning devices 10 feet, 100 feet, and 200 feet behind your vehicle.

questions.question: Improperly loaded cargo can:

options.text: Hurt or kill the driver during a sudden stop
Make it easier to stop a vehicle

questions.correctAnswerText: Hurt or kill the driver during a sudden stop
questions.explanation: Cargo that is not properly secured is dangerous. Loose cargo can fall during a sudden stop and injure or kill the driver.

questions.question: When driving at night, what should you NOT do?

options.text: Make sure your glasses are clean

questions.explanation: Do not wear sunglasses at night because they make it harder to see. If you wear eyeglasses, keep them clean. Make sure you are rested before driving at night.

questions.question: If air pressure drops between ____, a low pressure warning signal should have already turned on.
questions.explanation: A low pressure warning signal should turn on before air pressure drops to between 55 and 75 psi. This signal can be a light, buzzer, or wig wag.

questions.question: Extremely hot temperatures can cause:
questions.explanation: Hot air expands, so tire pressure increases in hot weather. This can cause tire failure. Always check your tire pressure during hot weather trips.

questions.question: If driving in extremely hot weather and your tire air pressure is too high, what should you do?

options.text: Let air out of the tire.
Stop and let the tires cool down before driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and let the tires cool down before driving.
questions.explanation: Hot air expands, so tire pressure rises in very hot weather and can become dangerous. Stop and let your tires cool. Do not release air from the tires, as the pressure will drop too low once they cool.

questions.question: How many hours of sleep does an adult need each day to stay alert?
questions.explanation: Most adults need eight to nine hours of sleep each night to stay alert and drive safely.

questions.question: Why are roads especially slippery when rain first starts?

options.text: The rain mixes with oil on the road.
The water has nowhere to go.

questions.correctAnswerText: The rain mixes with oil on the road.
questions.explanation: When rain first starts, it mixes with oil drippings on the road that have not yet washed away. This creates a very slippery surface.

questions.question: Why are roads especially slippery when it first starts to rain?

options.text: Water mixes with oil and grease on the road.
Tires are not made for wet weather.
Water has not yet absorbed dirt and grease.

questions.correctAnswerText: Water mixes with oil and grease on the road.
questions.explanation: When rain first starts, it mixes with oil and grease on the road surface that has not yet washed away. This creates a slick film.

questions.question: When exiting your vehicle, how many points of contact must you keep with the vehicle at all times?
questions.explanation: You must face the vehicle and keep three points of contact at all times when exiting. On a bus, you must hold the handrail. Exiting incorrectly may cause automatic failure of the basic control skills test.

questions.question: Why should your mirrors show part of your vehicle as well as the road behind you?

options.text: Seeing only the road in the mirror might make the driver sick.
Seeing part of your vehicle gives you a reference point.
It is illegal to show only the road in the mirrors.
You need to see the reflection of surrounding vehicles on the trailer.

questions.correctAnswerText: Seeing part of your vehicle gives you a reference point.
questions.explanation: Seeing part of your vehicle in the mirrors helps you judge how close other drivers and objects are to your vehicle.

questions.question: On any uphill grade, gravity will:
questions.explanation: Gravity slows your vehicle down on uphill grades. You may need to shift to a lower gear to climb a steep hill.

questions.question: Joggers wearing headsets:

options.text: Are usually aware of what is happening around them.
May not be aware of what is happening around them.
Usually do not have music playing.

questions.correctAnswerText: May not be aware of what is happening around them.
questions.explanation: Be careful around joggers and cyclists wearing headphones. They may not hear traffic and may not know you are there.

questions.question: If cargo is shipped on a flatbed trailer or a trailer without sides, it must be:

options.text: Loose to allow it to shift when the vehicle turns.
Heavy enough so it will not shift.

questions.explanation: Cargo on a flatbed or open trailer must be securely tied down so it does not shift or fall off while the vehicle is moving.

questions.question: Are wheels with welding repairs safe to use?

options.text: Yes, if a professional did the repairs.
Yes, if the repair looks solid.

questions.explanation: Wheels or rims that have been welded are not safe to use. They must be replaced before the vehicle is driven.

questions.question: When backing up, what is best to do?

options.text: Use only the passenger's side mirror.
Turn toward the passenger's side when possible.

questions.explanation: Back up slowly and use mirrors on both sides of your vehicle. Use a helper to watch your blind spots when possible. Agree on a signal to mean "stop."

questions.question: If you are disqualified from driving, what must you do?

options.text: The state will notify your employer.
You must tell your employer within two business days.
You must tell your employer within one month.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must tell your employer within two business days.
questions.explanation: You must tell your employer within two business days if your license is suspended, revoked, canceled, or if you cannot drive.

questions.question: During the vehicle inspection test, which is NOT required?

options.text: Show where the dipstick is located.
Show that engine oil is at a safe level.
Show that oil is below the refill mark.

questions.correctAnswerText: Show that oil is below the refill mark.
questions.explanation: You must show where the dipstick is and that the oil level is safe and above the refill mark. You do NOT show that oil is below the refill mark.

questions.question: If another vehicle is tailgating you, what should you do?
questions.explanation: If you are going slower than other traffic, stay in the right lane when possible.

questions.question: When can brakes get out of adjustment?

options.text: When brakes on one side are used more than the other side.

questions.explanation: Hot brakes are likely to get out of adjustment. Use proper braking techniques to keep your brakes from overheating.

questions.question: What should you know about a cardboard box on the road?

options.text: It may contain something heavy that could damage your vehicle.
You should drive off the road to avoid it.

questions.correctAnswerText: It may contain something heavy that could damage your vehicle.
questions.explanation: Any object on the road is dangerous. Something that looks harmless like a cardboard box could contain something hard or heavy that damages your vehicle.

questions.question: How can a commercial vehicle driver use a cell phone while driving?

options.text: They can use any cell phone.
They can only use a hands-free cell phone.
They can only use one on rural roads.
They can use one at night.

questions.correctAnswerText: They can only use a hands-free cell phone.
questions.explanation: Commercial vehicle drivers cannot use handheld cell phones while driving. They can only use hands-free phones.

questions.question: What does the suspension system do?

options.text: Holds up the vehicle and its load.
Keeps the load the proper distance behind the driver.
Lightens the load on the tires.

questions.correctAnswerText: Holds up the vehicle and its load.
questions.explanation: The suspension system holds up the vehicle and its load and keeps the axles in place. A damaged suspension system is very dangerous.

questions.question: When visibility is poor and you are near other drivers, what lights should you use?
questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights when it is hard to see and other drivers are near you, such as at dawn, dusk, or in bad weather. High beams can make it hard for other drivers to see.

questions.question: What is the minimum tread depth for front tires?
questions.explanation: Front tires must have at least 4/32 of an inch of tread depth in major grooves. Other tires must have at least 2/32 of an inch.

questions.question: You should always be able to stop within:

options.text: Your view of the road ahead.
A minute of hitting the brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your view of the road ahead.
questions.explanation: You must be able to stop your vehicle within the distance you can see ahead. Slow down whenever you cannot see far enough ahead.

questions.question: When driving, your mirrors should:

options.text: Not be used, as they are distracting.
Not be used unless there is traffic.

questions.explanation: Check your mirrors often. This helps you know what is happening around your vehicle at all times.

questions.question: A cargo van carrying a heavy load is usually taller than when it carries a light load.
questions.explanation: A cargo van sits lower when carrying a heavy load. When carrying a light load, the van sits higher and needs more overhead space.

questions.question: When backing a truck, you should:

options.text: Only use the side mirrors on the driver's side.

questions.explanation: Backing is dangerous because you cannot see everything behind you. Check both mirrors often when backing. Use a helper when possible.

questions.question: Which of the following is a good rule to follow when making a turn?

options.text: Use your arms to get the attention of other drivers.
Turn off your turn signal before entering the turn to avoid confusing other drivers.

questions.explanation: Signal well before you turn. Keep your signal on while turning. Turn it off after you finish the turn. This warns drivers behind you of your plans.

questions.question: When starting the engine of a truck with a trailer, how can you tell if the Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) is not working?

options.text: The yellow light on the rear of the trailer will stay on.
The red light on the trailer will flash three times and then stay on.
All the rear lights on the trailer will flash and then shut off.
The blue light near the driver's door will light.

questions.correctAnswerText: The yellow light on the rear of the trailer will stay on.
questions.explanation: Trailers with ABS have a yellow warning light on the back left side. If this light stays on after the engine starts, the ABS is broken and needs repair.

questions.question: To correct a drive-wheel braking skid, a driver should do all of the following, except:

options.text: Remove your foot from the brake pedal.
Turn quickly in the direction of the skid.
Countersteer after the vehicle is back on course.

questions.explanation: To stop a drive-wheel braking skid, release the brakes to let the wheels roll again. Steer in the direction you want to go. Then steer back the other way to prevent skidding in the opposite direction. Do not speed up.

questions.question: When should you slow for a curve?
questions.explanation: Always slow down before you enter a curve. Slowing down while in the curve may cause your vehicle to skid.

questions.question: To determine if a vehicle can handle a load, you should:

options.text: Know the tire rating for the front tires only.
Start driving and see if the vehicle is handling well.

questions.explanation: Know your vehicle's weight limits and suspension rating. Do not overload your vehicle. Make sure the load does not exceed what your vehicle can safely carry.

questions.question: Roads are slippery when it first begins to rain because:

options.text: The fresh rain mixes with oil on the roadway.
The water has nowhere to go.

questions.correctAnswerText: The fresh rain mixes with oil on the roadway.
questions.explanation: Roads are very slippery when rain first starts because the water mixes with oil and grease on the road. This creates a slick layer. As more rain falls, this layer washes away.

questions.question: If you see a distracted driver on the road, what should you do?
questions.explanation: When you see a distracted driver, keep plenty of distance between your vehicle and theirs. Maintain a safe following distance.

questions.question: Which one is NOT a sign that a driver is getting tired?
questions.explanation: Signs of driver fatigue include trouble focusing, frequent blinking, heavy eyelids, yawning, rubbing eyes, daydreaming, trouble remembering the last few miles, missing exits, trouble keeping your head up, drifting from your lane, following too closely, hitting rumble strips, and feeling restless or irritable. Feeling hungry is not a sign of fatigue.

questions.question: Before backing up, what should you do?

options.text: Drive backward as fast as possible to finish quickly.
Get out and walk the path to check for obstacles.
Use only the passenger side mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get out and walk the path to check for obstacles.
questions.explanation: Before you back up, get out of the vehicle and walk along your path to look for obstacles. Back up slowly and check both mirrors as you go.

questions.question: While driving, your mirrors should:

options.text: Only be used when changing lanes.

questions.explanation: Check your mirrors regularly while driving to stay aware of traffic around you. Mirrors also help you spot problems with your own vehicle.

questions.question: A loud noise may mean a tire has failed.
questions.explanation: A loud "bang" sound can mean a tire has failed. There is a short delay between the tire failure and when your vehicle reacts. You might think the noise came from another vehicle.

questions.question: When you press the brake pedal, air pressure activates a switch and:

options.text: Turns on the low pressure warning light.
Turns off the low pressure warning light.

questions.explanation: In a vehicle with air brakes, pressing the brake pedal pushes air pressure that activates an electric switch. This switch turns on the brake lights.

questions.question: Emergency equipment like a fire extinguisher is:

options.text: Only needed for vehicles carrying hazardous materials.

questions.explanation: All commercial motor vehicles must have emergency equipment. This includes spare fuses, three red reflective triangles or flares, and at least one charged and rated fire extinguisher.

questions.question: The front of an enclosed trailer should:
questions.explanation: When inspecting an enclosed trailer, check the front for damage like cracks, bulges, or holes.

questions.question: After you stop during the stop/start maneuver, you should:

options.text: Keep the vehicle in first gear.

questions.explanation: When parking during the stop/start maneuver, apply the parking brake. Shift into neutral or park. Park parallel to the curb and do not block any driveways or intersections.

questions.question: When doing pre-trip inspections, you should:

options.text: Do them the same way each time.
Check items in a different order each time.
Not inspect every item each time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do them the same way each time.
questions.explanation: Always do pre-trip inspections the same way every time. This habit helps you remember to check every important part and avoid missing something.
